# T6.09: HEVC through VideoToolbox, vttest and Parsec

`libnvencvt` registers two encoders: `org.nvenc.videoencoder.avc` (avc1) and **`org.nvenc.videoencoder.hevc`**
(hvc1), same factory; the session codec comes from the codec type VideoToolbox passes to the factory. For HEVC the
session opens `enc.c` with `ENC_HEVC`, builds the format description from VPS + SPS + PPS
(`CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromHEVCParameterSets`) and reports `kVTProfileLevel_HEVC_Main_AutoLevel`. The frame
path (Annex B -> length-prefixed NAL units, sync emit in real-time mode) is shared. `NVENCVT_NO_HEVC` registers H.264
only.

- Injected (`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`): `vttest hw hvc1 1920 1080 60` -> our encoder, 60/60 frames decode, 56.76 dB
  (min 50.23); 3840x2160 -> 49.66 dB (min 42.15). vttest's own frame generation limits it to ~27 fps at 4K for both
  codecs.
- Through the plugin (`NVMTL_NVENCVT=vttest,parsecd`, the bundle's `libnvencvt.dylib` updated): `vttest hw hvc1` gets
  `org.nvenc.videoencoder.hevc`, 56.76 dB; avc1 still ours (53.90 dB); an unlisted process gets no hardware HEVC
  encoder (-12908).
- **Parsec** (client set to H.265, 2026-10-18 13:24): host log `encoder = Hardware`, `codec = h265`, 3840x2160,
  **encode latency L 4.4-5.3 ms** at 30-35 fps (H.264 with our encoder: 4.7-4.9 ms).
